newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: CRICKET-SRI LANKA BOWL NZ CHEAPLY IN ONE-DAY MATCH.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-SRI LANKA BOWL NZ CHEAPLY IN ONE-DAY MATCH.

text.p: Sri Lanka were well-placed to win the second and final one-day cricket international against New Zealand at the Basin Reserve on Thursday.
The World Cup holders were clinically efficient when dismissing New Zealand for 201 in 49.2 overs, with left arm seam bowler Chaminda Vaas particularly impressive.
Vaas picked up the excellent figures of four for 26 after his captain Arjuna Ranatunga decided to make use of the early seam and swing assistance for his bowlers.

New Zealand were in serious trouble at 28 for three inside eight overs, and only a fine 56 from Chris Cairns, 39 from wicketkeeper Adam Parore and lower order resistance from Gavin Larsen, who made 26, and Simon Doull, 18, enabled the home side to top 200.
Vaas headed the Sri Lankan attack, but he was ably helped by teenage seamer Nuwan Zoysa, who accounted for opener Nathan Astle and Stephen Fleming to finish with two for 47.
Offspinner Muttiah Muralitharan also picked up two wickets at a cost of 32 runs from his full allocation of 10 overs.
Sri Lanka won the first match in the series in Christchurch on Tuesday by six wickets when they passed New Zealand's 201 for nine in just 35.5 overs.
The first game of the three-match series was rained out in Auckland last weekend.
